resources.string: Detects which app comes to the foreground so AppLocker can show its lock screen. It cannot read anything on screen.
Phase 0 build: the permission setup works, but apps are not blocked yet. Blocking arrives in Phase 1.
Protection: OFF — blocking is not built yet (Phase 0)
Protection stays OFF until the missing permissions are granted.

Android blocks some permissions for apps installed from a file. Open app info, tap the three-dot menu, choose Allow restricted settings, then come back. These labels are not yet verified on the Pixel 11.
Needed to detect when a locked app opens and show the lock screen. AppLocker only sees which app is in front, never what is on screen.
Skipped for now. AppLocker plans to show its lock screen through the Accessibility service, which needs no extra permission. The final choice is made in Phase 1.
Needed as a backup detector and to count time spent in locked apps.
Needed to count steps in your earn window. AppLocker only reads steps and never writes health data.
Health Connect is not available on this device.
If the prompt does not appear, open Health Connect settings and allow Steps for AppLocker there.
Needed so Android does not stop blocking and step syncing in the background.
Needed for the notification Android requires while protection is running.
How AppLocker uses your health data
AppLocker reads your step count from Health Connect to decide when locked apps may open. The data stays on this device. It is never written back, uploaded, or shared.
